concepts.title: Order and Degree of Differential Equations
concepts.definition: The order of a differential equation is the highest derivative present, and the degree is the power of that highest derivative after the equation is freed from radicals and fractions in derivatives. In d2y/dx2 + p dy/dx + qy = 0 the order is 2 and the degree is 1.
concepts.key_idea: Order counts differentiations, degree counts powers: (d2y/dx2)^3 + dy/dx = 0 has order 2 and degree 3. Degree is defined only when the highest derivative appears with a whole-number power.
question_patterns: Determine the order and degree of the differential equation ({a} d2y/dx2)^2 + dy/dx = 0.
What is the order of the differential equation d3y/dx3 + {a} d2y/dx2 = 0?
Find the degree of (dy/dx)^{a} + y = 0.
Why can degree be undefined for some differential equations?
State the order and degree of y'' + ({a} y')^3 = 0.

concepts.title: General and Particular Solutions
concepts.definition: A general solution of a differential equation contains as many arbitrary constants as the order of the equation; fixing those constants with initial conditions gives a particular solution. Solving dy/dx = {a}x gives y = {a}x^2/2 + C generally, and y = {a}x^2/2 + {b} particularly when y(0) = {b}.
concepts.key_idea: Number of arbitrary constants in the general solution equals the order of the equation. Each initial condition removes one constant, ending at the particular solution that models the actual situation.
question_patterns: Solve dy/dx = {a}x and find the particular solution with y(0) = {b}.
How many arbitrary constants does the general solution of a second order differential equation contain?
Distinguish between general solution and particular solution.
Find the solution of dy/dx = {a} that passes through the point (0, {b}).
Evaluate the particular value of y = a x^2 / 2 + c0 at x = {x} when a = {a} and c0 = {b}.

concepts.title: Forming Differential Equations by Eliminating Constants
concepts.definition: To form a differential equation from a family of curves, differentiate the general equation as many times as there are arbitrary constants, then eliminate the constants between the equations. A family y = A e^x + B e^(-x) needs two differentiations to remove A and B, yielding y'' = y.
concepts.key_idea: The number of differentiations needed equals the number of arbitrary constants: one constant gives a first order equation, two constants give a second order equation.
question_patterns: Form the differential equation representing the family y = A e^(x) + B e^(-x).
Form the differential equation of the family of curves y = {a}x^2 + {b}x + C.
How many times must you differentiate y = A cos x + B sin x to eliminate the constants?
Eliminate the arbitrary constant a from y^2 = {a}ax.
Represent the family of all circles centred at the origin by a differential equation.

concepts.title: Variable Separable Equations
concepts.definition: A first order equation is variable separable when its terms can be rearranged so that all y terms sit with dy and all x terms sit with dx. Integrating both sides then gives the general solution: dy/y = dx integrates to ln y = x + C, that is y = C e^x.
concepts.key_idea: Separation converts a differential equation into two ordinary integrals. Growth and decay models dy/dt = ky all separate this way, and their solutions are exponentials.
question_patterns: Solve the differential equation dy/dx = {a}y.
Solve dy/dx = y/x by separating variables.
Find the general solution of dy/dx + {a}y = 0 and describe its graph.
A population grows at a rate proportional to its size; write and solve the model.
Separate the variables in dy/dx = {a}x y^2 and integrate.

concepts.title: Mathematical Modeling with Differential Equations
concepts.definition: Modeling translates a physical or economic situation into a differential equation, solves it, and interprets the solution back in context. Radioactive decay, cooling, population growth and continuous compounding all produce first order separable models whose solutions are exponentials.
concepts.key_idea: The modeling cycle is: name the variables, write the rate statement as a differential equation, solve with initial conditions, then validate against the real behaviour. The exponential solution N = N0 e^(kt) covers growth when k is positive and decay when k is negative.
question_patterns: A substance decays at a rate proportional to its amount; model the decay and give the solution.
Write the differential equation for Newton's law of cooling and explain its terms.
Money grows at {r} percent compounded continuously; model the balance with a differential equation.
Why does the same model dy/dt = ky describe both growth and decay?
For N = N0 e^(kt) with k = -{r}, what does the sign of k tell about the process?

worked_examples.q: Solve dy/dx = 2x with the initial condition y(0) = 5, and state which solution is general and which particular.
worked_examples.a: Integrating gives y = x^2 + C, the general solution with one arbitrary constant matching the order one equation. Applying y(0) = 5 fixes C = 5, giving the particular solution y = x^2 + 5.

worked_examples.q: Form the differential equation of the family y = A e^(2x) by eliminating the constant.
worked_examples.a: Differentiate once: dy/dx = 2A e^(2x). Since A e^(2x) = y, the equation becomes dy/dx = 2y, a first order equation, exactly matching the one eliminated constant.
